A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DMDR and provide readable text, equations, tables and figures. All pages were inspected, including v1's appendices. Much of that appendix material is incorporated into v4's main text, allowing relocation to be distinguished from removal.

before.justification: v1 reports original text-to-image experiments, benchmark comparisons, component and RL-algorithm ablations, diversity measurements and qualitative results, including appendix comparisons.

after.justification: v4 reports original text-to-image results, training-strategy and component experiments, and an additional class-conditional ImageNet study.

M1.justification: v1 uses dynamic DMD for a reward-free cold start before joint DMD/RL training. v4 introduces Reward-Tilted Distribution Matching (RT-DM): rewards from complete few-step trajectories become fixed weights on DMD gradients during the initial stage (Section 2.4). This changes early optimization; DynaDG, DynaRS and the subsequent joint stage are retained.

E1.justification: The original t2i-2M, ShareGPT-4o-Image, GenEval and DPG_Bench coverage remains. v4 extends evaluation beyond text-to-image generation to class-conditional ImageNet 256×256 generation using SiT (Section 4, Table 6), introducing a distinct dataset and conditioning task.

E2.justification: v4's system comparison adds reproduced multi-step ReFL baselines for SDXL and SD3, plus DMD2-PSO for SDXL. Its new Table 1 compares joint training against multi-step RL and RL followed by distillation. Conversely, v1's RL-only DPO/GRPO controls are absent from v4; sequential ReFL remains tested in Figure 4.

E3.justification: Dynamic-strategy evaluation changes from CLIP/HP scores at 1K and 2K iterations to DPG measurements at earlier checkpoints. New protocols include training/test reward and DPG trajectories, a 1024×1024 timing comparison with local batch size 16 on H100, and one-step ImageNet evaluation across CFG/RL configurations using FID, recall, precision and Inception Score. These are distinct experimental designs, not matched-setting performance comparisons.

E4.justification: v4 adds RT-DM versus continued RT-DM versus joint-training analysis, reward-model ablations, an RL-loss-weight sweep, and a CFG/RL diversity study. Reward-hacking analysis now includes held-out reward and DPG trajectories. v1's fixed '-Dynamic' control, RL-algorithm qualitative grid and ShareGPT LPIPS diversity comparison are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version documents repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for its performance results. v1's raw/smoothed reward fluctuations describe within-training variability, not uncertainty across repeated experiments; v4 introduces no corresponding statistical uncertainty procedure.

E6.justification: Reported DMDR results change across the main tables: SD3-M DPG rises from 84.96 to 85.30 and GenEval from 0.64 to 0.65, under the revised method/training description. Numerous strategy, sensitivity and ImageNet results are added. Rankings also become more nuanced: v4's added SDXL ReFL baseline exceeds four-step DMDR in HP score, 33.1874 versus 32.9832. The earlier LPIPS results are removed.

T1.justification: v4 adds a mathematical definition of the reward-tilted teacher target and an asserted reward-weighted KL-gradient expression (Equation 4). The original DMD gradient remains. This is a localized formal extension; no theorem or proof establishes the new target/gradient equivalence.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion add RT-DM and reward-informed initial distillation as central contributions, replacing v1's reward-free dynamic cold-start contribution. Joint DMD/RL benefits and teacher-surpassing performance remain headline claims. v1's explicit emphasis on image-free training is dropped.

C2.justification: v4 introduces explanations for RT-DM saturation, loss-weight-dependent reward hacking, and CFG/RL acting as distribution 'density sharpeners.' It interprets DMD regularization as manifold projection and presents reduced diversity as potentially desirable. The earlier reward-model-bias/scaling limitation and proposed connection between reduced diversity and weaker DPO/GRPO gains are omitted.

D1.justification: v4 specifies 1.5K training steps per stage, a default RL weight of 0.5, hardware/batch details for timing, and SiT initialization and DINOv2 reward information. It removes v1's explicit baseline CFG settings and 512×512 ablation default. These are documentation changes; omitted settings do not establish changed execution. The code URL remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 substantially expands positioning through works such as Flash-DMD, TwinFlow and PSO and a new reward-model discussion. v1's Appendix A is largely relocated into Section 5. The novelty framing also changes: v1 acknowledges Diff-Instruct++ integrating RL during distillation, whereas v4 groups it with work focused on RL after distillation.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and method narrative are extensively rewritten around an explicit two-stage framework, with diagnostic experiments embedded in the method discussion. Related work moves near the end and absorbs Appendix A; appendix visual comparisons move into the main results. Author and affiliation information also changes.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout. The pipeline diagram is redrawn, diagnostic plots and a multipart ablation table are introduced, and system-table columns are restructured. v1's appendix comparison grids are consolidated into v4 Figure 8, while several original showcase and ablation displays are removed.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens the empirical argument with held-out reward/DPG trajectories, loss-weight and reward-model controls, and comparisons against RL-improved baselines. These make the central synergy claim easier to assess. Gains are tempered by removing in-domain LPIPS evidence and some controls, losing setting details, and introducing an unexplained reward-tilted target/gradient equivalence. The net improvement is supported but qualified.
